headline: MSFT presses to fresh highs near $505 as commercial backlog grows 84%
summary: Shares extended their post-earnings rally to a range of $490-$505.56 on Aug 27, with the commercial backlog up 84% YoY to $678B and Azure past $100B in annual revenue. Roughly 97 analysts remain overwhelmingly bullish, with an average price target of $589-592 — implying meaningful further upside even after the ~30% post-earnings run.

headline: Kirin's C$2.5B all-cash buyout of Jamieson now a signed definitive agreement
summary: Jamieson signed a definitive agreement to be acquired by Tokyo-based Kirin Holdings for C$45.75/share in cash, valuing the deal at ~C$2.5B (~US$1.4B) — a 27% premium to the pre-talks 20-day VWAP. The board approved unanimously; closing is targeted for Q4 2026 subject to shareholder, court and regulatory approval. Jamieson (Youtheory, Progressive, Iron Vegan, Smart Solutions, Precision) will run as a wholly-owned Kirin subsidiary.

headline: TD's Q3 profit jumps 38% to $4.6B, shares rise on the beat
summary: Fiscal Q3 profit came in at $4.62B, up from $3.34B a year ago, on revenue of $16.89B (from $15.30B) — helped by record earnings in the Canadian retail business and wholesale banking. Diluted EPS reached $2.74 (adjusted $2.77) vs. $1.89 a year earlier, adjusted ROE improved to 16% (from 14.4%), and credit provisions eased to $917M (from $971M). Shares rose on the print, extending the run that had already drawn raised price targets from Barclays, BofA and CIBC.

headline: DRI Healthcare exits EKTERLY royalty for ~US$178M after Chiesi's KalVista buyout
summary: DRI exercised its contractual put option on the EKTERLY royalty and received a ~US$178M put price after Chiesi Group completed its acquisition of KalVista Pharmaceuticals, terminating that royalty right. The stock fell 3.76% on Aug 14 as investors weighed the portfolio shift, closing near $17.99 on Aug 19. This follows record Q2 results (total income +13% YoY to $50.1M, adjusted EBITDA +40% to $42.6M, 92% margin) with FY26 guidance reaffirmed at the high end.

headline: RBC posts $6.0B Q3 profit, tops estimates, shares rise pre-market
summary: Q3 profit reached $6.02B, up from $5.41B a year ago, on revenue of $18.54B (from $16.99B), driven by strength in wealth management, capital markets and commercial banking. Diluted EPS was $4.23 (adjusted $4.28) vs. $3.75 a year earlier — ahead of the ~C$4.06 street estimate. Credit provisions rose to $1.00B (from $881M). The board raised the quarterly dividend to $1.76/share, payable Nov 24. This follows Barclays' Aug 21 target hike to C$300 from C$260.

headline: Wheaton's record H1 revenue rides gold near $4,300/oz
summary: H1 2026 revenue hit a record US$1.8B (operating cash flow US$1.4B) as gold held near US$4,300/oz and Wheaton's average realized gold-equivalent price rose 78% YoY; silver production climbed 14.5% to 6.4M oz. The stock has gained ~20% over the past year (52-week range $90.95-$165.76) and Berenberg raised its target to $180 (Buy); bank targets across the Street now span $157-$179.43.

headline: Amazon whipsaws after Q3 miss and weak Q4 guidance, closing down modestly after a volatile session
summary: Following its mixed Q3 2026 report (revenue and EPS both slightly missing despite record margins and 39% AWS growth), Amazon shares were volatile into the Oct30 close: premarket down as much as 7% to around $226, with an intraday low near $224, before recovering through the session to close at $240.35 (-1.41% day-over-day from Oct29's $243.79). The partial recovery came amid a broader AI-capex selloff across tech (Intel fell sharply the same day), with investors drawing a sharper distinction between AWS's genuine growth strength and concerns over Amazon's heavy capex and negative free cash flow.

headline: Netflix slides ~11% in two sessions after Wells Fargo's rare Underweight downgrade
summary: Wells Fargo analyst Steven Cahall downgraded Netflix from Equal Weight to Underweight (a rare sell-equivalent call) and slashed his price target to $57 from $80, citing weakening user engagement and a softer H2 2026 original-content slate. The firm's base case projects a 21% YoY decline in viewing hours across the platform's top 100 originals, with Netflix slipping in the Nielsen Gauge and facing potential margin-expansion headwinds and rising subscriber-churn risk into next year. Shares extended a multi-day slide to close at $71.79 (-10.7% on Sep 21), part of a stock that is now down ~26% for 2026 — a stark divergence from the broader Sep 21 tech rally that lifted most of the fund's other growth names.

headline: Alphabet slips as AI capex concerns offset cloud strength
summary: Shares fell over 1% on Aug 26 as investors weighed reiterated plans for a significant step-up in fiscal 2027 capital spending against Q2's 82% Google Cloud growth. BNP Paribas reiterated an Outperform rating and $420 target, citing Alphabet's positioning across AI-driven advertising and cloud, and highlighted a new AI-accessibility partnership with Clearlake Capital. The tension between elevated AI infrastructure spend and monetization remains the key debate on the stock.

headline: Berkshire beats on earnings; Abel adds to Alphabet stake
summary: Berkshire reported EPS of $6.02 vs. $5.13 expected on Aug 8. Under new CEO Greg Abel, the company added roughly $17B more to its Alphabet position in mid-August and increased its Delta stake, continuing a string of sizeable equity purchases.

headline: Constellation's profit quadruples in Q2, but shares slip on valuation
summary: Q2 (reported Aug 12) profit jumped to $274M from $56M a year earlier on revenue of US$3.18B and EPS of US$17.32, yet the stock still fell 3.19% on Aug 17 (from $3,089 to $2,991 CAD) after a run of +21% over three months left valuation stretched (P/E ~63x). Jefferies raised its target to C$3,294 (from C$3,185, Buy) citing broad AI-tooling adoption and token-cost tracking across the portfolio; consensus 12-month target sits near C$3,951.

headline: MercadoLibre holds a Street-wide Buy rating with ~14% upside seen from here
summary: Shares trade around $1,991, within a 52-week range of $1,495-$2,548.50; all 19 covering analysts rate the stock Buy (none Sell), with an average 12-month target of $2,265 implying roughly 14% upside. That follows the Q2 report (revenue +49.8% YoY to a record $10.17B, fintech payment volume above $100B, active users +30%) even as margins compressed on heavier logistics and fintech investment — 2026 is shaping up as another heavy capex year for Mercado Envios and Mercado Pago.

headline: Sea Limited surges after Q2 revenue jumps 48% on Shopee and Monee strength
summary: Q2 GAAP revenue reached $7.8B (+48.1% YoY) with net income of $458M, powered by Shopee e-commerce, the Monee fintech unit and Garena gaming. Shares climbed from ~$102-105 in mid-July to ~$114-115 by Aug 10 (+13.6% on the day). Benchmark, Morgan Stanley and Barclays all raised targets post-earnings even as TD Cowen trimmed its own.

headline: Shopify gives back its post-earnings rally, now down ~26% from the August peak
summary: After running hard on a well-received Q2 report (Aug 5) and rallying toward the top of its 52-week range (~$213 CAD in late August), Shopify has cooled sharply on profit-taking — down roughly 26% over the past month with consecutive daily declines (-4.2% Aug 31, -3.6% Sep 1) and no fresh negative catalyst on the fundamentals. Shares remain a premium-multiple growth name and stay sensitive to momentum shifts in tech/e-commerce; Q3 results (guided to ~30%+ revenue growth) are the next real checkpoint.

headline: US-Canada trade talks collapse; 50% tariffs hit $20B of Canadian goods
summary: Two weeks of talks broke down late Friday Aug 21 — hours after Trump said negotiators had "pretty much" struck a deal — and the US pushed ahead with 50% tariffs on roughly $20-28B of Canadian exports (wine, hockey sticks, cement, furniture, plastics, plywood, electrical equipment), about 5% of Canada's US-bound exports. PM Carney called the move a "miscalculation" and says Canada will match the tariffs dollar-for-dollar starting Sept. 8. Despite the news, the TSX has continued to climb on commodity strength; watch for knock-on effects at wood/building-products and industrial names in the Canadian and Small Cap mandates (e.g. Stella-Jones, TFI International).

headline: Meta sinks 7% on legal charge and runaway AI capex despite a revenue beat
summary: Meta reported Q3 2026 results after the close Oct 21: revenue rose 26% YoY to $64.6B, beating estimates, but operating income fell 37% as a $9.89B legal charge (tied to a New Mexico ruling imposing a $25B penalty, which Meta is appealing) and surging AI infrastructure spending hit the bottom line -- capex of $33.94B exceeded operating cash flow for the first time since 2012. Shares fell about 7% to close near $648.85 on Oct 22, Meta's third straight 5%+ post-earnings drop since its 2012 IPO, as investors grow more skeptical of the payoff from its AI spending spree even as the company touted its new Muse AI agent.

headline: Alphabet sinks on rare earnings miss and negative free cash flow despite Cloud revenue more than doubling
summary: Alphabet's Q3 2026 report (Oct28 after close) marked the company's first top-and-bottom-line miss in nearly four years: revenue of $127.6B (vs ~$128B consensus, still +25% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $2.67 (vs $3.02 est.), with GAAP EPS of $2.12 down from $2.87 a year ago partly on an unrealized loss on its SpaceX stake. Free cash flow swung to -$9.1B (vs +$2.7B expected) as capex and inventory investment rose and the company paid a $5.2B EU Commission fine. Google Cloud revenue more than doubled (+103% YoY to $30.7B, backlog $561B) and full-year capex guidance held at $195-205B, but investors focused on the cash-flow miss -- shares fell sharply (~10-12% per multiple reports) on Oct29, dragging the broader market lower even as Microsoft's own strong Azure-driven beat (+48% YoY) landed the same evening.

company: Nasdaq slides as Alphabet's earnings miss outweighs Microsoft's beat
headline: Stocks slip as Alphabet sinks on a rare profit miss and negative free cash flow, even as Microsoft's Azure beat impresses
summary: Stocks fell Thursday Oct 29 as Alphabet's first earnings miss in nearly four years overshadowed a strong Microsoft report: the Nasdaq Composite dropped roughly 1.3-1.6%, the S&P 500 fell about 0.5% to roughly 7,690-7,707, and the Dow slipped about 0.5%. Alphabet shares sank 10-12% after a profit miss and a swing to negative free cash flow (partly on a $5.2B EU fine), even though Cloud revenue more than doubled. Microsoft, by contrast, beat estimates with Azure growth of 48% but saw a more muted reaction given a 34% run-up into the print. The divergence highlights investors drawing sharper lines between AI spending that's paying off (Azure, Roper, Spotify) and spending that's raising cash-flow concerns (Alphabet, Meta). Amazon reports after today's close -- the next test of the AI-capex narrative.

company: AI-capex selloff spreads across tech, Intel hit hardest
headline: Broad tech selloff on AI-spending worries drags Nasdaq lower as Intel plunges, even as Amazon partly recovers
summary: A broader AI-capex selloff hit tech stocks Friday Oct30, following a week of mixed hyperscaler earnings (Meta's legal charge, Alphabet's cash-flow miss, Amazon's weak guidance). Intel shares fell sharply (reported ~29-30% by some sources) amid the same spending-scrutiny theme, while Amazon -- down as much as 7% premarket -- recovered through the session to close only modestly lower. The pattern reinforces the week's broader narrative: investors are increasingly discriminating between AI infrastructure spending that shows a clear near-term payoff (Microsoft's Azure, Roper) and spending that is pressuring cash flow and margins (Meta, Alphabet, Amazon).
